setup: Serve the web fixtures before running evals 2 and 3: `python3 -m http.server 8765 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory evals/fixtures/orbit-site` and `python3 -m http.server 8766 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory evals/fixtures/tallyfox-site`. Give each run its own copy of evals/fixtures/quillmate for eval 1. Keep the servers running for the whole run (e.g. wrap each in a restart loop) and tell executors not to stop them.

evals.name: repo-quillmate
evals.prompt: hey, we're launching Quillmate (our AI meeting notes app) on Product Hunt on Oct 6 (2026). The code is at {REPO}. Can you go through the repo and tell me if it's ready for the launch and what we need to fix before then? I'm based in Madrid btw.
evals.expected_output: A NOT READY verdict with evidence-backed blockers: the 'Please upvote us' banner, localhost metadataBase and missing /og.png, no gallery screenshots, 128px logo below the 240x240 thumbnail, a public OpenAI endpoint without auth or rate limits; majors such as card-required trial and long sign-up form, no analytics/ref attribution, no privacy/terms. Includes a validated launch kit (tagline <=60) and the go-live time 09:01 CEST in Madrid.
expectations: Flags the 'Please upvote us' Product Hunt banner (app/components/ProductHuntBanner.tsx) as a violation of Product Hunt's rules, and says the upvote ask must be removed or replaced
Identifies that metadataBase is hard-coded to http://localhost:3000 in app/layout.tsx, breaking social previews in production
Notes that /og.png referenced in the Open Graph metadata does not exist in the repo
Flags that the only logo (public/logo.png, 128x128) is too small for Product Hunt's 240x240 thumbnail
Flags that the repo has no product screenshots that could be used for the Product Hunt gallery
States that the Product Hunt gallery needs at least 2 images (1270x760 recommended)
Flags the public /api/summarize OpenAI endpoint (no auth, no rate limit) as a launch-day cost or abuse risk
Flags the broken sign-up/checkout flow: Stripe's success_url points to a /welcome route that doesn't exist and/or no account is ever created (the password is ignored)
Flags the credit-card-required trial and/or the long sign-up form (phone, company, role, team size) as friction for Product Hunt visitors
Flags missing analytics and/or missing attribution of Product Hunt traffic (ref=producthunt / UTM)
Flags that there are no privacy policy or terms pages (footer links point to '#')
Presents a Product Hunt tagline (in the reply or launch kit) of 60 characters or fewer that says what the product does, with no hype words or emoji
States that the launch goes live at 12:01 AM Pacific Time, which is 09:01 in Madrid (CEST), on October 6
Gives an overall verdict that the product is not ready to launch as-is

Names at least one Product Hunt eligibility rule the maker must confirm that can't be seen in the code: posting account at least a week old, no launch of the same product in the last 6 months, or no upvote services/vote groups
Saves a written readiness report file in the outputs directory with a verdict and, for each blocker, file:line evidence and a fix
Flags the critical vulnerability in next@15.3.2 (e.g. via npm audit) or marks the dependency audit as unverified when the registry is unreachable
Flags the hype headline 'The Ultimate Revolutionary AI Note-Taking Experience 🚀' as unsuitable
Notes that the core product (meeting bot, notes view, Slack delivery) isn't in the repo and asks where it runs
Describes its evidence accurately: does not claim real OpenAI/Stripe/Resend calls or production checks it didn't make, and scopes findings to where they occur

evals.name: url-orbit-waitlist
evals.prompt: Our landing page is running at http://localhost:8765/ (it's the same build that'll go to orbit.ai). We want to put Orbit on Product Hunt this Friday — can you check the page and tell me if it's good to go for PH?
evals.expected_output: A NOT READY verdict: the page is waitlist/early-access only (not eligible for featuring) so the launch should wait until the product is usable (use a Coming Soon page meanwhile); /demo, /pricing and /terms return 404; no Open Graph/Twitter tags, no meta description, no favicon; hype + emoji headline unsuitable as a tagline. Correctly notes Plausible analytics is present. Mentions 12:01 AM PT.
expectations: Identifies that the page only offers a waitlist / early-access sign-up (no usable product) and explains this makes it ineligible or very unlikely to be featured on Product Hunt
Recommends not launching this Friday until the product is usable, and suggests an alternative such as a Product Hunt Coming Soon/teaser page to collect followers
Notes that the lead time is already short or past due for a Friday launch (scheduling in advance and/or the posting account needing to be at least a week old)
Detects that the 'Try the demo' link (/demo) returns 404
Detects that the Pricing link (/pricing) returns 404
Detects that the Terms link (/terms) returns 404
Flags the waitlist form's Formspree endpoint (formspree.io/f/xyzabc) as a likely placeholder that could lose sign-ups
Flags the missing Open Graph image/tags and Twitter card
Flags the missing meta description
Flags the missing favicon/app icon and that there is no source for a 240x240 thumbnail

Flags the hype/emoji headline ('The world's most revolutionary AI platform. Ever.') as unsuitable and proposes a tagline of 60 characters or fewer, without hype or emoji, that uses only claims present on the page
Correctly reports that analytics (Plausible) is present rather than claiming the page has no analytics
Mentions that Product Hunt launch days start at 12:01 AM Pacific Time
Gives an overall verdict that the page is not ready for a Product Hunt launch
Does not suggest asking for upvotes and does not invent product facts (pricing, metrics, testimonials) in any drafted copy
Flags the unverifiable claims on the page ('Join 2,000+ people', 'Infinite memory', 'startups to Fortune 500') as needing proof or softening
Drafts a description or first comment that uses only claims present on the page and marks unknowns as TODOs

evals.name: listing-tallyfox
evals.prompt:
I'm about to submit Tallyfox to Product Hunt next Thursday (Oct 1). Site is at http://localhost:8766/ (staging copy of tallyfox.app). Here's my draft listing, can you review it against PH's rules and give me a fixed version I can paste?

Name: Tallyfox — The Smartest Invoice Tracker for Freelancers
Tagline: The best invoicing app ever made — revolutionize your freelance business 🚀🔥
Description: Tallyfox is the ultimate invoicing solution for freelancers, designers, developers, writers, consultants and agencies of every size who are tired of chasing late payments. Our cutting-edge platform tracks every single invoice you send, automatically emails polite reminders before and after the due date, shows your cash flow in a beautiful dashboard, sends receipts the moment clients pay, supports Stripe, PayPal and bank transfers, and lets you customize everything with your own branding. Join 1,200 happy freelancers today!
Launch tags: Productivity, Fintech, Freelance, SaaS, Invoicing
Pricing: Paid
Thumbnail: icon-512.png (512x512)
Gallery: hero.png (1270x760)
First comment: Hey Product Hunt! 👋 I'm Dana, the maker of Tallyfox. Please upvote us and share with your friends — every upvote counts 🙏 We built Tallyfox because freelancers lose hours every month chasing payments.
Shoutouts: Stripe, Notion, Figma, Vercel
Promo: 50% off Pro for 3 months, code PRODUCTHUNT50
Tweet for launch day: We're live on Product Hunt! Go upvote Tallyfox 🦊 https://www.producthunt.com/posts/tallyfox
evals.expected_output: Each field is checked against the form's limits and rules with counts: name 55/40, tagline 75/60 + hype + emoji, description 528/500, 5 tags (max 3), 4 shoutouts (max 3), 1 gallery image (min 2), promo missing expiration, first comment and tweet ask for upvotes, pricing should be 'Paid (with a free trial or plan)' because the site has a Free plan. A corrected, paste-ready listing within limits. No false claims about the site, which has OG tags, icons and a pricing page.
expectations: Flags the name as over the 40-character limit and proposes a name of 40 characters or fewer
Flags the tagline as over 60 characters and/or using hype and emoji, and the proposed replacement tagline is 60 characters or fewer with no emoji
Flags the description as over the 500-character limit and provides a rewritten description of 500 characters or fewer
Does not present 260 characters as the current description limit (mentioning that only ~260 characters are visible before truncation is fine)
Flags that 5 launch tags exceed the maximum of 3 and proposes 3 or fewer
Flags the first comment's request to upvote as against Product Hunt's rules
The rewritten first comment contains no request to upvote
Flags the launch-day tweet ('Go upvote Tallyfox') as asking for upvotes and rewrites it without asking for upvotes
Does not guess the Product Hunt post URL in the rewritten tweet (uses a placeholder or tells the user to insert the real link)
Flags that the gallery has only 1 image while at least 2 are required, and recommends adding more (3+, 1270x760)
Flags that the pricing option should be 'Paid (with a free trial or plan)' (or otherwise reflect the Free plan) because the site offers a free plan
Flags that the promo is missing an expiration date
Flags that 4 shoutouts exceed the maximum of 3, and the final recommendation lists 3 or fewer
The rewritten description uses only facts from the draft or the site (e.g. drops 'agencies of every size', keeps custom branding as a Pro feature)
Does not falsely claim that the site lacks Open Graph tags, a favicon/icons, or a pricing page
Gives the go-live time (12:01 AM Pacific Time on Thursday Oct 1) and says the launch must be scheduled now because it's only days away
Flags at least one visitor-path defect on the staging site (e.g. 'Log in' goes to /signup/, the Google button links back to sign-up, or the Crisp ID '6f1c-demo' is a placeholder)
